annotation.title_clean: The Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure (Security Requirements for Relevant Connectable Products) Regulations 2023
annotation.title_en: The Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure (Security Requirements for Relevant Connectable Products) Regulations 2023
annotation.authors_or_issuer: UK Secretary of State, Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
named_instruments_referenced: Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure Act 2022
annotation.summary_en: UK statutory instrument under the Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure Act 2022 setting cybersecurity requirements for manufacturers of consumer connectable products: no default passwords, vulnerability reporting contacts, published minimum security update periods, and statements of compliance. Deemed compliance via ETSI EN 303 645, ISO/IEC 29147, Japan JC-STAR or Singapore labelling. Not AI-specific.
key_provisions_or_claims: Unique, non-guessable passwords required; no default passwords
Manufacturers must publish a vulnerability reporting contact and acknowledge reports
Defined minimum security update period must be published and not shortened
Deemed compliance through ETSI EN 303 645, ISO/IEC 29147, JC-STAR STAR-1 or Singapore CLS labels
Statements of compliance required and retained for 10 years or the support period; excepted products include medical devices and EV charge points
